title: Optionals and async Swift
summary: Return an optional safely, then diagnose a forced unwrap in a lookup.

scenario.briefing: A campus app looks up the first positive reading and may find nothing. Represent absence without crashing.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

misconceptions.description: Force unwrapping the first element of the input.
misconceptions.testDescription: The loop returns the first positive value and nil otherwise.
misconceptions.feedback: values.first! traps on an empty array and ignores positivity. Iterate and return nil when nothing matches.

misconceptions.description: Filtering and then force unwrapping the result.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Writing values.filter { $0 > 0 }.first! so an empty match traps.
misconceptions.feedback: filter followed by first! still traps when no value matches. first without the bang returns an optional the caller can handle.

misconceptions.description: Catching the trap later instead of preventing it.
misconceptions.feedback: Force unwrapping an optional is not catchable. Handle nil with guard let or the nil-coalescing operator before multiplying.

misconceptions.description: Treating force unwrap as a safety check.
misconceptions.feedback: The ! operator asserts that a value exists and traps otherwise. It does not check or provide a default.

sections.title: Swift functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare parameter and return types: func add(_ left: Int, _ right: Int) -> Int { left + right }. Array<Int> or [Int] stores an ordered collection, and Dictionary stores key-value pairs. Async functions and actors structure concurrent work.

sections.title: Swift errors and tools
sections.body: A throwing function uses throws, and callers use do/catch or try?. Optionals are not errors; they represent a legitimate absence. Swift Package Manager resolves dependencies, swift build compiles, swift test runs tests, and Xcode provides the IDE.

steps.title: The missing dictionary key
steps.prompt: This code traps when the key is absent. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: A dictionary lookup returns an optional.
The crash is at the forced unwrap, not the print.
Catching a trap after the fact is not possible.
Use nil-coalescing or guard let before multiplying.

fixes.label: Use guard let balance else { return } before multiplying.
Wrap the force unwrap in a do/catch.

steps.explanation: A dictionary lookup returns an optional. The nil-coalescing operator supplies a default instead of trapping.

steps.title: Optionals and async Swift
hints: An optional return type documents absence.
guard let exits the current scope on nil.
Force unwrap traps instead of supplying a default.
await suspends without blocking the thread.

statements.label: An optional return type documents that absence is possible.
guard let exits the current scope when the value is nil.
Force unwrapping turns a failed lookup into a safe default.
An async function can suspend without blocking its thread.

steps.explanation: Optionals make absence part of the type. Async functions suspend at await points and actors serialize mutable state.
